mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 6.0% for two consecutive months, it indicates a weakening labor market that prompts the Federal Reserve to adopt a more accommodative stance, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE has exceeded 6.0% for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and a rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals a contraction in real demand and rising inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as the Federal Reserve may be forced to tighten policy.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where HOUST declines and CPIAUCSL rises, or the Rank IC falls below -0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a period of rising industrial production (INDPRO) above 105.0, a concurrent decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 6.0% signals a strong labor market and robust supply-side growth, which typically supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: strong supply growth with labor market tightness
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO > 105.0 and UNRATE < 6.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) over the past month indicates strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS has increased over the prior month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation that may lead the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0, or the Rank IC is below -0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS) and a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals a shift in consumer spending patterns from durable goods to services, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the economy faces a demand imbalance.
regime_hint: demand shift from housing to services
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where RSAFS increases and HOUST declines, or the Rank IC falls below -0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a period of declining industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0, a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.0% signals a weakening supply chain and labor market, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: supply contraction with labor market slack
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO < 105.0 and UNRATE > 6.0, or the Rank IC is below -0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.
